newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's JSE considers second backup network.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's JSE considers second backup network.

text.p: The Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) said on Monday it was considering a second backup network for its share trading system after the existing support network failed on Friday, costing nearly five hours of trade.

JSE president Roy Andersen said brokers were connected to two "token rings", linking key buildings where brokers are guaranteed access to the system. One of the token rings was in use and the second was the backup ring.
"We are considering having another backup system. We are checking if the loads are properly distributed. There is a feasibility study under way to determine that," Andersen told Reuters.
Friday's disruption was the third since the exchange completed the move to a fully automated screen trading system in June.
Trade was extended by an hour to 1700 GMT on Friday.
Andersen emphasised that the Johannesburg Equities Trading (Jet) itself had not failed.
"This had nothing to do with Jet. We have had no problems with it. In one of the token rings there was a hardware failure and the backup ring did not perform up to standard," Andersen said.
Dealers said the disruptions were frustrating, but they welcomed the JSE's decision to extend trade by an hour on Friday.
"It is annoying. The system keeps going down. This is bad advertising for the country. You can't deal overseas orders. People think we are Mickey Mouses," one dealer said.
"But it was most welcome that trade was extended by an hour on Friday," he added.
Other dealers said the system was acceptable, though occasional problems were unfortunate.
"I think it is a good system. It has been tested in Chicago and they made a few changes for our market but nothing is perfect. These (problems) come and go," he said.
The Jet system was acquired by the JSE from the Chicago Stock Exchange.
